steps.frontier-goal: You command Ming. Prepare Liaobei, then advance into Yehe. Win by controlling 16 non-Korean regions at New Year, capturing an enemy capital, or reaching 3 prestige.
steps.opening-move: All factions share the wheel. Move 1 for free; moving 2 lets one chosen opponent draw 2, while moving 3 lets every opponent draw 2. Move 1 this turn.
steps.prepare-hand: After moving, you may perform one hand action and the landing action in either order. First recruit troops for Liaobei.
steps.recruit-source: Regular troops must be raised in your homeland. Select Liaobei.
steps.recruit-action: Recruit Army: discard 1 card to raise six level-2 troops or two level-4 Sichuan troops. Choose Recruit Army.
steps.recruit-payment: Cards also pay for actions. Spend Silver, which has no special effect, and keep Mandarin Duck Formation. Use the magnifier to inspect a card; on touch screens you can also long-press.
steps.recruit-troops: Choose six level-2 troops to provide infantry for the river crossing.
steps.farm-action: Military Farming draws 2 cards and raises one level-2 regular troop. Replenish the front and your hand.
steps.farm-target: Select Liaobei for the new troop.
steps.reclaim-action: Reclaim adds 1 population to each of up to 5 controlled regions, within their caps. Liaodong currently has equal population and troops; increase its population to prepare for tax income.
steps.reclaim-target: Select Liaodong. A region with more population than troops provides 1 tax card at Midyear.
steps.opening-finish: Your hand action, reclaiming and military farming are complete. Finish the wheel action; Mongolia acts next.
steps.midyear: Jin reaches Midyear. The wheel must stop at Midyear and New Year. After the active player resolves one landing action, all players collect tax from unsieged regions with more population than troops; Ming draws 5 additional canal cards. Then check character conditions and roll once per defeat marker.
steps.hand-limit: Ming now exceeds its 15-card hand limit. Discard the highlighted six cards at the start of your turn, preserving Artillery Technology and Mandarin Duck Formation.
steps.battle-move: Move 1 to dispatch and attack. This turn cross from Liaobei into Yehe.
steps.upgrade-first: First develop Artillery Technology with your hand action, then use the wheel to attack.
steps.upgrade-card: An armament is played as a hand action and costs one additional discard. It stays in play. Each developed Artillery Technology adds 1 to artillery rolls and raises its training cap.
steps.upgrade-payment: Spend Silver for the additional cost. The technology card will stay in play.
steps.dispatch-action: Discard 1 card to command up to 6 troops. Infantry and artillery move 1 region; cavalry move 2. Entering enemy territory triggers battle.
steps.dispatch-payment: Pay with this card and preserve Mandarin Duck Formation.
steps.dispatch-troops: The river into Yehe has width 2; artillery does not use that width. Select the two newly recruited level-2 infantry and one level-1 artillery, then confirm.
steps.dispatch-target: Select Yehe. Its Mongol defender must now decide whether to evade.
steps.defender-response: Defending cavalry can evade into other controlled regions. Mongolia fights. Normal defense is 3, but its cavalry armor raises this to 4: four roll points are needed per damage. The tactics phase follows.
steps.tactic-card: Tactics are played during battle, normally one per battle. Level-2 infantry use eight-sided d8 dice. Mandarin Duck Formation temporarily changes these to ten-sided d10 dice; the troops themselves remain level 2. Select and confirm the card.
steps.battle-roll: Both sides resolve artillery, cavalry, then infantry. Highest-level troops take damage first. Each damage lowers infantry or cavalry one level; at zero they are removed. Artillery cannot absorb damage and does not count toward victory. Start the rolls.
steps.occupy: More surviving non-artillery troops wins; ties favor the defender. The Mongol defenders are destroyed. Occupy to increase Ming's controlled regions. A field-battle loser also places a defeat marker on an eligible character for Midyear judgement.
steps.battle-finish: Ming controls Yehe. Uncommitted troops remain in Liaobei. Finish your turn.
steps.opponent-round: Mongolia and Jin move the shared wheel. Your next turn starts from its new position.
steps.diplomacy-move: Move 1 to weaken Mongol relations and hire reinforcements behind the front.
steps.diplomacy-action: Diplomacy affects up to 3 regions adjacent to your controlled territory, placing or removing control markers. Homeland without a control marker, regular garrisons and Korea are excluded. Choose diplomacy.
steps.diplomacy-target: Outer Khalkha has a reverse Mongol friendship marker permitting passage and garrisoning; the front represents vassal control. Select it to remove the Mongol friendship marker.
steps.diplomacy-finish: Mongolia's friendship marker is removed. The region remains neutral. Finish diplomacy.
steps.hire-action: The first discard hires two level-2 mercenaries into a controlled region. Further hires during this action cost one card per troop.
steps.hire-target: Deploy the two mercenaries in Liaodong.
steps.diplomacy-round-finish: Diplomacy and hiring are complete. Finish the wheel action.
steps.save-hand: New Year maintenance and upkeep require cards. Keep your hand and decline another hand action this turn.
steps.new-year: Mongolia reaches New Year. First draw tribute according to controlled Korean regions. Ming then chooses each fortification's maintenance, followed by upkeep, chronology and characters. Korea has separate draw and discard piles.
steps.maintain-shanhai: Shanhaiguan, Ningyuan and Jinzhou each cost 2 cards; the inner wall costs 2 and the outer wall 6. Abandonment ruins that defense and removes its special effects. Keep Shanhaiguan and reserve the rest for troop upkeep.
steps.maintenance-first-card: Select the first Shanhaiguan maintenance card.
steps.maintenance-second-card: Select one more to complete the two-card cost.
steps.abandon-jinzhou: Abandon Jinzhou maintenance to conserve cards.
steps.abandon-outer-wall: Abandon outer-wall maintenance. Ruin markers appear on the defenses.
steps.upkeep-yehe: Each unsupported troop needs one discarded card or must be removed. Ming regulars receive no local support in non-Han regions.
steps.upkeep-xianxing: Korean garrisons receive no local population support. Discard this card to retain Xianxing's troop.
steps.other-upkeep: Jin pays for its own Jianzhou upkeep. Wait for Jin, then continue at Liaobei.
steps.upkeep-liaobei: Liaobei has four more troops than population. Select these four support cards.
steps.upkeep-pyongyang: You may instead remove troops. Preserve cards for later actions by removing the Pyongyang mercenary.
steps.upkeep-hanseong: Remove the Hanseong mercenary and keep your cards.
steps.upkeep-liaodong: Liaodong needs one more support. Remove this level-1 artillery, preserving the artillery at Yehe.
steps.claim-year: The next chronology compares territorial growth. Taking Yehe qualifies Ming; ties favor the faction later in the old order. Discard half your hand, rounded up, to claim this year's card and 1 prestige, or decline for the next faction. Claim it now.
steps.chronology-first-card: With 5 cards, discard 3 to claim the chronology. Select this Korean Silver.
steps.new-order: The new chronology sets turn order and character candidates: Mongolia, Ming, then Jin. Mongolia plays a character before you.
steps.year-character: Characters are separate from your hand and have lasting effects. Your army has grown; choose Yang Gao to command up to 10 troops when dispatching or attacking, unaffected by other character effects. Inspect his card with the magnifier.
steps.year-ready: Jin completes its character choice. Mongolia takes the first turn of the new year, followed by Ming.
steps.training-move: Move 1 to recruit and train. Your saved card can pay for training.
steps.training-action: Discard 1 card for up to 4 recruit or train actions. Each recruit raises one level-2 regular troop; each training raises one troop one level. Train the artillery at Yehe.
steps.training-payment: Pay this Korean card. It goes to Korea’s discard pile.
steps.training-target: Each troop can gain at most one level per turn. Artillery's cap depends on armaments. Your developed technology permits this Yehe artillery to advance from level 1 to level 2.
steps.training-finish: Each additional discarded hand card allows one more training action.
steps.finish: You completed recruitment, supply, battle and the Midyear/New Year cycle. Continue pursuing territory and chronology cards: reach 3 prestige, capture an enemy capital, or control 16 non-Korean regions at New Year.
steps.chronology-third-card: Discard the third card to claim this year’s chronology.

basic.title: Introduction: from recruitment to New Year
basic.description: Learn recruitment, battle, supply, Midyear and New Year in one continuous match.

steps.frontier: Attack Yehe this turn. First use Military Farm in Liaobei to reinforce the frontier.
steps.selectFarmRegion: Regular troops may only be established in homeland regions. Select Liaobei.
steps.wheelMove: Choose an opponent to draw two cards and move the wheel two spaces. At Military Farm, draw two cards and establish one level-2 regular troop. Move two spaces.
steps.wheelOpponent: Choose Jin to draw two cards.
steps.chooseTarget: Select Yehe as the raid target.
steps.chooseRaid: Raid: discard one hand card to attack, without dispatching. Select Raid.
steps.payRaid: Discard Silver to pay for this raid and keep Mandarin Duck Formation for the battle. Inspect a card with the magnifying glass or press and hold on touch screens.
steps.confirmRaidPayment: Confirm discarding the selected Silver card.
steps.battleOpen: Both sides reveal their troops. The uppermost pips show level: level 1 rolls a d6, level 2 a d8, and level 3 a d10. Liaobei and Yehe are separated by a river, giving battle width 2; artillery ignores the boundary limit.
steps.playTactic: Mandarin Duck Formation cannot be used during siege attack or defense; it raises your infantry die level by one in battle. This is a field battle. Play the tactic card.
steps.resolveBattle: Select the fourth Liaobei troop to commit four troops, then click Start battle.
steps.battleResult:
Resolve artillery, cavalry, then infantry, with both sides acting simultaneously in each stage. Every three points deals one damage. Infantry and cavalry lose levels and are removed at level zero.

The side with more surviving troops wins, excluding artillery; ties favor the defender. Check the dice and survivors, then decide how to occupy Yehe.
steps.occupy: After winning, the attacker may occupy or withdraw without changing control. Choose to occupy Yehe.
steps.finish: Supremacy victory requires at least 16 controlled regions outside Korea at New Year. The tutorial ends here; continue this match.

attackAndBattle.title: Attack And Field Battle
attackAndBattle.description: Raid starts from a hand action, then flows into field battle, tactics, damage assignment, and retreat handling.

steps.actionOverview: The right side lists Ming's four same-level faction actions: Raid, Recruit, Grant Pardon, and Drive Tiger. Choose 1 each turn.
steps.chooseAction: Now choose Raid. Rule: discard 1 hand card to make an attack; dispatch is not allowed.
steps.payRaid: Select Chahar on the map, then select 1 hand card and confirm payment.
steps.borderWidth: The attack moves from Keshiketeng into Chahar. Read battle width 3.
steps.battleOpen: Entering an enemy region starts a field battle. Reveal both sides, then open the tactic window.
steps.tacticWindow: Click Cavalry Charge, then click Play Tactic Card to confirm.
steps.battleDamage: Now click Rear Guard to resolve the field battle. Resolve artillery, cavalry, then infantry; each 3 points deals 1 damage.
steps.battleResult: The field battle is resolved: Chahar troops decrease from 1 to 0. Then read the surviving troops and the next post-battle action.
steps.retreatAndDefeat: The losing side chooses either Rear Guard or Rout.
steps.postBattleChoice: Now use the post-battle panel to choose the closing action.
steps.finish: Field battle, retreat, and post-battle handling are complete. Return to the map result.

siege.title: Siege And Occupation
siege.description: Siege covers defender city withdrawal, city battle resolution, and the post-victory choice between siege and occupation.

steps.overview: Enter the Shanhaiguan city battle. Resolve the defender choice and city battle, then choose to besiege, occupy, or withdraw.
steps.defendCity: Choose Hold City. The defender moves troops and population into the city.
steps.cityBattle: After the defenders enter the city, click Rear Guard. Resolve artillery, then cavalry and infantry; cavalry takes -1 here.
steps.cityResult: The city battle is resolved. Choose to besiege, occupy, or withdraw in the post-battle panel.
steps.postBattleOutcome: Besiege keeps Jin in control and preserves the city garrison; occupation gives Ming control and clears the garrison; withdrawal gives up the occupation and returns surviving troops to an adjacent friendly region. Choose one outcome, then choose its target.
steps.besiegeResult: Besiege complete: Jin still controls Shanhaiguan, the city garrison remains, and Ming's besieging force stays outside the city.
steps.occupyResult: Occupation complete: Shanhaiguan is now controlled by Ming and the city garrison is cleared.
steps.withdrawResult: Withdrawal complete: Jin still controls Shanhaiguan; surviving troops return to an adjacent friendly region.
steps.finish: Post-battle processing is complete; besieging, occupying, or withdrawing determines Shanhaiguan's control, city state, and where surviving troops go.

retreatAndRout.title: Retreat And Rout
retreatAndRout.description: The field-battle loser chooses between rear guard and rout.

steps.overview: Enter the losing side's retreat choice: Rear Guard or Rout.
steps.routResult: After routing, the top player information gains 1 defeat marker, and the source region no longer keeps the routed force.
steps.finish: The map shows troop results; the top player information shows defeat markers.

cavalryPlunder.title: Cavalry Plunder
cavalryPlunder.description: Cavalry can switch to plunder: take artillery/cavalry counterfire first, then plunder population with surviving cavalry and retreat.

steps.overview: Enter the cavalry plunder choice. Resolve counterfire, then population, cards, and retreat.
steps.plunderResult: Plunder is complete: target population is lower, cavalry retreats, and the deck changes are synced.

cavalryEvasion.title: Cavalry Evasion
cavalryEvasion.description: Defending cavalry can leave a field battle for an adjacent friendly region without being treated as routed.

steps.overview: Enter the defending cavalry evasion choice.
steps.chooseEvasion: Click the highlighted adjacent friendly region to move the defending cavalry.
steps.evasionResult: The defending cavalry has left the original battle; the original battle continues.
steps.finish: Evasion changes troop position without a defeat-retreat penalty.

neutralInvasion.title: Neutral Invasion
neutralInvasion.description: When you attack an unoccupied neutral region with population, neutral defenders are generated for the battle.

steps.overview: Enter neutral-region battle resolution. An unoccupied neutral region with population generates neutral defenders.
steps.resolveNeutral: Now click battle resolution. Neutral defenders are created from Tumed's population.
steps.neutralResult: Neutral defenders now occupy Tumed; the attacker did not defeat them, so control stays neutral.
steps.finish: Neutral control changes only if the attack breaks through.

waterDispatch.title: Water Dispatch
waterDispatch.description: Ming can dispatch through anchor-region sea routes; cavalry dispatch can reach farther, but each sea route still commits at most 2 troops.

steps.overview: Enter water dispatch. Ming moves troops through sea routes between anchor regions.
steps.chooseWaterTarget: Click Dongjiang as the water destination. Each sea route commits at most 2 troops, and the route cannot switch back to land.
steps.waterBoundary: The water boundary has battle width 2, so at most 2 troops fight there.
steps.finish: Water changes route and battle width; the normal battle rules still resolve.

wheelSharedCost.title: Wheel Branches And Development Actions
wheelSharedCost.description: Longer shared-wheel movement refills opponents and lands the turn in attack, dispatch, diplomacy, or hiring systems.

steps.overview: Enter the 3-space wheel branch. Both opponents draw 2, and the turn lands on attack / dispatch.
steps.chooseMove: Click the highlighted Attack / Dispatch sector on the wheel.
steps.drawResult: After the wheel moves 3 spaces, read the Mongol and Later Jin hands: each gains 2 cards.
steps.payDispatch: Select 1 hand card and confirm the payment.
steps.finish: The discard is complete. You can continue by selecting troops on the map.

wheelReclaim.title: Reclaim
wheelReclaim.description: Wheel Reclaim directly adds population to a controlled region.

steps.chooseMove: Click the highlighted Reclaim sector on the wheel.
steps.result: Reclaim is complete: Xuanfu population increases by 1.

wheelMilitaryFarm.title: Military Farm
wheelMilitaryFarm.description: Draw cards and establish a regular troop through Military Farm.

steps.overview: Military Farm: draw two cards and establish one level-2 regular troop.
steps.chooseMove: Click the highlighted Military Farm sector on the wheel.
steps.result: Military Farm is complete: 1 level-2 regular troop appears in Xuanfu, and the hand is replenished.

wheelRecruitTrain.title: Recruit and Train
wheelRecruitTrain.description: Pay a hand card, choose Recruit or Train, and see the troop change on the board.

steps.overview: Move 1 more space from Military Farm to reach Recruit / Train.
steps.paymentRule: Discard 1 hand card to perform up to 4 Recruit or Train actions
steps.chooseMove: Click the highlighted Recruit / Train sector to enter its choices.
steps.payInitial: Select 1 hand card and confirm the discard.
steps.actionsRule:
-  Recruit action: directly create 1 level-2 regular troop.
-  Train action: rotate a troop up 1 level; each troop may be raised only 1 level per turn.
steps.chooseTrainingTarget: Choose Xuanfu's level-1 artillery. Artillery Technology is level 2, so this troop can be raised to level 2.
steps.trainingResult: Xuanfu's artillery has risen from level 1 to level 2; this counts as 1 action.
steps.homelandRule: and must be established only in homeland (dark-colored) regions.
steps.artilleryRule: (Artillery's level cap must be raised by armaments.)
steps.chooseRecruitTarget: Choose one homeland region from the available regions.
steps.recruitResult: One level-2 regular troop was created in the chosen homeland region.
steps.extraTrainingRule: You may discard hand cards for extra Train actions; each discarded card adds 1 extra Train action.
steps.chooseExtraTraining: Click Extra Training, then discard 1 more hand card.
steps.payExtra: Select 1 hand card and confirm the discard.
steps.chooseExtraTrainingTarget: Choose an untrained regular troop in Xuanfu and raise it from level 2 to level 3.
steps.extraTrainingResult: The extra discard added 1 Train action; this Xuanfu regular troop has risen to level 3.
steps.finishAction: Click Finish Recruit / Train to end this resolution.
steps.result: Recruit, Train, and extra Train are listed in this action summary; wheel and hand actions can continue.

armamentUpgrade.title: Armament Upgrade
armamentUpgrade.description: Armament upgrade spends hand cards and updates the armament level on the live board.

steps.actionOverview: Armament Upgrade: play an armament card, discard 1 hand card, and upgrade that armament.
steps.chooseAction: Now click Artillery Technology in hand.
steps.payCards: Play Artillery Technology, discard 1 hand card, and confirm.
steps.result: Artillery Technology rises from level 1 to level 2.
steps.finish: Armament Upgrade is complete; later battles use level-2 Artillery Technology.

eventAction.title: Khan's Edict
eventAction.description: Khan's Edict is the Mongol faction action. It resolves through payment, effect choice, and result, with the discard and map change landing together.

steps.overview: Now enter the Mongol hand action.
steps.actionOverview: The right side lists three same-level Mongol faction actions: Raid, Horse Market, and Khan's Edict. Choose 1 each turn.
steps.chooseAction: Now click Khan's Edict. Discard 1 hand card, then perform Recruit / Train or Diplomatic Hiring without another payment.
steps.chooseEffect: Choose the source region, then choose Recruit / Train to enter its Recruit or Train choices.
steps.recruitTrainActionsRule:
-  Recruit action: directly create 1 level-2 regular troop.
-  Train action: rotate a troop up 1 level; each troop may be raised only 1 level per turn.
steps.recruitHomelandRule: and must be established only in homeland (dark-colored) regions.
steps.chooseRecruitTarget: Click one of the available homeland regions.
steps.recruitResult: One level-2 regular troop was created in the chosen homeland region.
steps.finishRecruitTrain: Click Finish Recruit / Train to end Khan's Edict Recruit / Train effect.
steps.result: Khan's Edict Recruit has resolved; check the action summary and map result.
steps.finish: Khan's Edict Recruit / Train effect is complete.

diplomacy.title: Diplomacy And Hire
diplomacy.description: Enter a real wheel diplomacy step and see control markers and hired troops resolve together.

steps.wheelEntry: Click the highlighted Diplomacy / Hire sector on the wheel.
steps.chooseTarget: The target must border a controlled region; homeland, Korea, and regions with regular troops are excluded.
steps.friendlyMark: Click Ningyuan to place a friendly marker. Troops may pass and station there, but it is not a controlled region.
steps.tributeMark: Flip the friendly marker to a vassal marker. A face-up marker counts as your controlled region.
steps.removeMark: Click Dongjiang and remove the rival control marker.
steps.finish: Diplomacy markers and hired troops are resolved.

yearAndCharacters.title: Midyear, New Year, And Chronology
yearAndCharacters.description: Midyear taxes, character checks, New Year maintenance, attrition, chronology scoring, and turn-order refresh form the yearly resolution.

steps.overview: Enter Midyear and New Year resolution: taxes, characters, fortifications, attrition, chronology, and turn order.
steps.advanceMidyear: Name one opponent to draw 2 cards, then move forward 2 spaces. Click the highlighted 2-space move, then choose an opponent.
steps.midyearTax: Midyear taxes are complete: read resources in the top player information; besieged regions do not collect tax.
steps.midyearCharacters: Character checks are complete: read characters and defeat markers in the top player information.
steps.advanceNewYear: After Midyear resolves, click the highlighted New Year position at the top of the wheel.
steps.newYearTribute: New Year tribute: the controller of each Korea region draws its marked Korea cards.
steps.newYearMaintenance: Click "Maintain fortifications as much as possible". The game automatically pays affordable maintenance costs in priority order; any fortification that cannot be maintained falls into ruin.
steps.newYearAttrition: Maintenance is complete: read attrition results on the map and in the top player information.
steps.chronologyScore: Chronology resolves: the highest score pays half the hand for the year's prestige, or passes.
steps.turnOrderRefresh: Chronology is complete: the year card, current actor, and character states refresh.

koreaSpecial.title: Korea And Special Map Rules
koreaSpecial.description: Korea, Hanseong, sea routes, and Shanhaiguan are map-specific rules that directly change play.

steps.overview: Enter the Korea, Hanseong, waterway, and Shanhaiguan special rules.
steps.koreaRegion: Tribute icons set the New Year draw; control decides who receives it.
steps.hanseongVp: Hanseong control is worth 1 prestige; read it in the top player information.
steps.waterLimit: Anchor water routes move at most 2 troops; cavalry cannot evade through water.
steps.newYearMaintenance: Click "Maintain fortifications as much as possible" to resolve New Year maintenance.
steps.koreaAttrition: Korea provides no population support; read Korean troop attrition after maintenance.
steps.shanhaiguan: Shanhaiguan is a city and a special border; intact is narrow, ruined is wider.
steps.finish: The Korea, Hanseong, waterway, and Shanhaiguan special rules are complete.

regionMask.title: Region Mask And Passage Editor

runtimePreview.title: Runtime Preview
runtimePreview.description: Read-only check for how the current workspace is consumed by runtime data.

runtimePreview.title: Read-Only Workspace Runtime Bridge
runtimePreview.descriptionSuffix: directly from the workspace to preview regions, centers, passages, and boundary rules at runtime without overwriting formal Qidahen data.
runtimePreview.stats: Centers {{nodes}} / Passages {{edges}} / Missing centers {{unresolved}} / Shared printed regions {{sharedPrinted}} / Missing authoritative guides {{missingGuide}} / Candidates {{candidates}}
runtimePreview.mapSectionTitle: Main map + region mask + runtime passage overlay
runtimePreview.reviewIntro: This page only proves that workspace output can be consumed by the runtime.
runtimePreview.reviewNote: It does not promote the current rough draft or detour workspace into formal boundary truth.

formalSharedPrinted.title: Formal Shared Printed Audit
formalSharedPrinted.description: This audits shared printed regions against the formal runtime contract, regardless of whether the current workspace only loaded a subset of regions.
formalSharedPrinted.note: The priority here is to expose any formal missing authoritative-guide blockers directly.
formalSharedPrinted.summary: Formal shared printed regions: {{count}}; missing authoritative guides: {{missing}}
formalSharedPrinted.guideComplete: Authoritative guides cover the current runtime mapping

sharedPrinted.title: Shared Printed Regions
sharedPrinted.description: If one printed region hits multiple runtime regions in the current workspace, it is listed here directly.
sharedPrinted.note: This reflects runtime/printed layering truth and does not mean the formal printed data has already been split.
sharedPrinted.previewHint: This thumbnail only shows how runtime ownership splits one printed region into multiple subregions. It does not mean the formal printed data has already been split.
sharedPrinted.candidateSummary: Recorded runtime-only guide candidates in this workspace: {{count}}.
sharedPrinted.empty: No multi-runtime shared printed samples are loaded in the current workspace.
sharedPrinted.guideComplete: Authoritative guides cover the current runtime mapping

runtimePreview.currentPassagesEmpty: No previewable region graph has been loaded yet.

extractionStats.title: Latest extraction stats · {{mode}}

mode.candidateReference: candidate reference from the current base map guide
mode.editableDraft: editable draft from the real base-map color line
mode.handDrawn: hand-drawn trace over the base map

extractionStats.candidateNote: Candidate verdict: only write to the reference layer, not the live boundary image; trace it into a closed boundary before generating regions.
extractionStats.draftNote: Draft verdict: written into the editable boundary layer, but still an open draft; broken segments may be discarded, and final output still needs per-region review.
extractionStats.readOnlyNote: Diagnostic verdict: the real base map has severe color collisions here, so this stays read-only and never writes into the boundary image.

regionMaskTool.saveFormalGuard: The formal workspace cannot save region output while the normality state is {{state}}. Export the review bundle, inspect each region, and finish all 5/5 manual approvals first; the temporary workspace can still save progress.

regionTruthWorkflow.sharedGuideAuditSummary: There are {{total}} formal shared-printed gaps right now; {{runtimeOnly}} of them are still runtime-only, so the current `regionIds` guide model cannot write them to disk directly.
regionTruthWorkflow.runtimeOnlyGuideGap: The current tool can only write guides to ids already present in current regions; the following gaps are runtime-only and cannot be saved directly through the current `regionIds` model: {{names}}

diagnostics.regionTolerance: Region base-color tolerance {{value}} (the wand uses seed-adjacent color plus boundary stopping; refine with the chain tool when needed)

workflow.candidateDiagnosticsVerdict: Auto extraction still cannot produce formal output: parameter scans on the real image reach at most {{matched}}/{{required}} independent seeds, and high tolerance hits UI/text/decorations. The fixed-color boundary draft is only a hand-repair starting layer and cannot be saved as final output directly.

recentGeneration.title: Latest batch generation results
recentGeneration.emptyHint: After one batch generation run, this panel tells you whether each region is generated, skipped for leakage, or not generated. Use it to see where the boundary pipeline still needs repair and which rough region drafts still need manual cleanup.

manualView.title: Manual editing and view
manualView.supportHint: Fine-line candidates only help you trace along long lines on the base map. They never write into the boundary image automatically and cannot replace a hand-drawn closed boundary.
manualView.autoSnapToContour: Snap the current red line to the fine-line contour
manualView.finalBoundaryHint: The red line is the final boundary used for region partitioning: the boundary image itself and manual edge additions merge into one obstacle dataset, and erasing only subtracts from that final red line.

selectedRegion.title: Selected region details
selectedRegion.purposeDiagnostic: Only used for sample guidance, magic-wand work, and chain boundary repair; it is excluded automatically from formal mask/graph exports.
selectedRegion.purposeFormal: The mask handles clicking and highlighting; the passage graph only expresses rules-level connectivity.
selectedRegion.truthDiagnostic: Diagnostic sample. It can validate direction but cannot replace formal region truth.
selectedRegion.truthAuthoritative: Explicit truth. The main pipeline consumes this region result directly.
selectedRegion.truthBootstrap: Heuristic bootstrap. It still needs chain refinement or promotion into explicit truth.
selectedRegion.sharedPrintedRuntime: This printed region currently maps to runtime regions: {{names}}.
selectedRegion.runtimeOnlyGuideBlocker: The blocker is not missing drawing work. The current guide target is still bound to `regionIds`, so runtime-only gaps like {{names}} cannot yet be written straight into the workspace authoritative guide file.
selectedRegion.metadataOnlyNote: This only writes workspace metadata and will not edit the formal `region-authoritative-guides.json` directly.
selectedRegion.notePlaceholder: Record why it belongs to this printed region and which formal proof step is still missing.
selectedRegion.authoritativeTruthNote: Explicit truth is consumed directly by the main pipeline and is written into the current workspace when saved.
selectedRegion.diagnosticTruthNote: Diagnostic temporary regions are not written into formal explicit truth; the Beijing sample should keep using the in-tool guide to validate direction.

passages.title: Passages
passages.description: Click an existing passage edge on the map, or drag from one region center to another to create an edge. The left panel only edits the currently selected passage.
passages.empty: No passages yet. Generate regions first, then use auto-fill by adjacency; special passages can still be drawn directly on the map.
